result.note: Tests the August 2026 duty-free raw sugar import decision, the supply-demand shortfall behind it, and the 20% ethanol blending link.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's sugar import decision of August 2026:
items: Mills and refiners were allowed to import 1 million metric tons of raw sugar duty-free until 31 October.
The duty-free window replaced the usual 100% tariff on sugar imports.
It marked India's first sugar import in nearly a decade.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct: on 20 August 2026 New Delhi allowed 1 million metric tons of raw sugar in duty-free until 31 October, in place of the usual 100% tariff. India went from exporting sugar to importing it within a single harvest.
questions.source: On Thursday, New Delhi allowed mills and refiners to import 1 million metric tons of raw sugar duty-free until October 31, replacing the usual 100% tariff.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's sugar supply position as reported in August 2026:
items: The harvest forecast of 27.9 million metric tons is below India's annual consumption of 28.5 million metric tons.
Before halting exports in May 2026, India had shipped the entire 1.59 million metric tons of sugar it had approved for export.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: India approved 1.59 million metric tons of exports but shipped only a little over 600,000 before halting trade in May. Output was initially expected at 30.95 million metric tons before the forecast was cut.
questions.source: The harvest is now forecast at 27.9 million, below annual consumption of 28.5 million.

questions.prompt: As reported in August 2026, Indian sugar mills diverted sugar into ethanol as India locked in petrol containing what share of ethanol?
questions.explain: India locked in petrol blended with 20% ethanol, and mills diverted around 3 million metric tons of sugar equivalent into ethanol. This diversion contributed to the shortfall that forced sugar imports.
questions.source: Mills diverted around 3 million metric tons of sugar equivalent into ethanol as India locked in petrol containing 20% ethanol.
